prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer's orange-clad legs (0.2–0.4 m away at the bottom) and extended right arm (0.4–0.7 m away) sit above a flat wooden work board on a tiled floor (roughly 0.8–1.2 m away), with an upright white shelf unit to the upper right and a cat behind it at about 1.0–1.4 m. A second person's hand appears at the top-left corner in frames 2 and 3 at roughly 0.6–0.8 m distance (about 0.4–0.6 m to the left of the wearer's right hand), while the wooden board, small wood blocks, sawdust, and hand saw remain within arm's reach of the wearer and the cat stays just beyond the upright divider. Across the five frames, the wearer's right hand moves forward and left across the board from frame 1 to frame 3 before retreating slightly in frame 4, and in frame 5 the camera turns and tilts up to the right, revealing darker, farther floor and furniture regions up to 2.0–3.0 m away while the left side of the board goes out of view. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the continuous luminance gradient clearly separates the elevated vertical edges of the white divider panels and the cat's silhouette from the underlying board and floor plane. However, the depth map is unreliable around the lower-right floor and near the saw in frames 1 through 4, where dark shadow-like dropouts make the floor appear artificially far, and it flattens thin objects like the saw blade and wood pieces into the board surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's lower body and right arm in the foreground (0.2–0.7 m away), a second person's hand or cardboard tube at the top left (0.6–1.0 m away), and a cat (1.0–1.4 m away) positioned to the right behind the white shelf panels and facing downward/right away from the camera wearer. The wearer's right hand operates within arm's reach in the lower-central foreground, separated by roughly 0.5 m from the cat to the upper right and 0.5 m from the top-left hand, while the wearer's torso and the second person's body remain out of view outside the top-down frame. Across frames 1 to 5, the foreground arm mask shifts from bottom-center toward the center-left and back down as the camera rotates right in frame 5, changing the cat's relative image position from a diagonal along the right edge to a horizontal orientation above the shelf panel. The map highlights the distinct contour of the cat and foreground body parts against a black background, which removes distracting sawdust and floor textures present in the RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable in classification and consistency: it omits the wooden board, shelf panels, wood blocks, and saw entirely, mislabels the wearer's black shoe and orange trousers as 'scissors' in frame 2, splits the wearer's limbs into multiple separate 'person' instances, misclassifies the cardboard tube in frame 1 as 'person' and the bright window in frame 4 as a 'person' mask, and relabels the cat as a 'dog' in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only 2D hand skeletons in magenta on a black background, showing the camera wearer's right hand in the lower-middle region (about 0.5–0.7 m from the camera) across all five frames and a second left hand at the top-left edge (about 0.6–0.8 m away, 0.4–0.6 m above and left of the right hand) in frames 2 and 3. In frames 1 through 4, the wearer's right hand is oriented with fingers pointing up and to the left as it sweeps wood pieces within arm's reach on the board, while the top-left hand rests on the cardboard tube with fingers splayed upward and its arm extending out of view past the top-left border. Across the sequence, the wearer's right-hand skeleton moves up and left from frame 1 to frame 3, shifts down and left in frame 4, and moves to the bottom-center pointing straight up in frame 5 as the camera turns rightward. This map makes the exact finger articulation and palm orientation of both hands much clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB frames (especially frames 1 and 4), even when the hands partially occlude the wooden block and tube. However, the map is incomplete and unreliable for broader scene understanding because it detects no body skeletons at all despite the visible legs and arms in the foreground, and it provides no spatial information about the cat, tools, or surrounding room layout.
